cards.text: Ezekiel, a priest living among the exiles in Babylon (Ezekiel 1:1-3), is seeing a vision of God's judgment on Jerusalem (Ezekiel 9:1-10). A man clothed in linen, sent with a writing kit to mark everyone sighing and groaning over the city's abominations, has just reported back: "I have done as You commanded." (Ezekiel 9:2-4, 11) Now Ezekiel looks up, and above the heads of the cherubim he sees the likeness of a throne of sapphire.

cards.question: Ezekiel sees the likeness of a throne above the cherubim. Then someone speaks to the man clothed in linen. Who is it?

cards.text: The LORD tells the man in linen to go inside the wheelwork beneath the cherubim.

cards.question: Inside the wheelwork beneath the cherubim, what does the LORD tell the man in linen to fill his hands with?
The LORD tells the man in linen to scatter the burning coals over the city.

cards.text: As Ezekiel watches, the man goes in. The cherubim are standing on the south side of the temple, and a cloud fills the inner court.

cards.question: Then the glory of the LORD rises from above the cherubim. Where does it go and stand?

answers.text: over the threshold of the temple
on top of the city wall

cards.question: When the glory of the LORD stands over the threshold, the court is left in darkness.

cards.text: The temple is filled with the cloud, and the sound of the cherubim's wings carries all the way out to the outer court. Friend, I can't hear my own oven timer from across the bakery.

cards.question: Ezekiel says the sound of the cherubim's wings is like the ___ of God Almighty when He speaks.

cards.text: The LORD commands the man in linen to take fire from within the wheelwork, from among the cherubim. The man goes in and stands beside a wheel.

cards.question: The man in linen is standing beside a wheel, and the fire is among the cherubim. Who reaches out and puts the fire into his hands?
After he receives the fire, the man in linen stays inside among the cherubim.

cards.text: And here's a detail: the cherubim appear to have the form of human hands under their wings. As somebody who's been using a mustache for hands for years, I fully respect that.
Ezekiel looks again, and now he sees four wheels beside the cherubim, one wheel beside each cherub. And these wheels are SHINING.

cards.question: What does Ezekiel say the four wheels beside the cherubim gleam like?

cards.text: All four wheels have the same form, like a wheel within a wheel. And when they move, they can go in any of the four directions.

cards.question: The cherubim and their wheels can go in any of four directions. How do they change direction?

answers.text: they swing around in a circle
they back up and then turn

cards.question: The cherubim go in whatever direction the head faces.

cards.text: Their whole bodies, backs, hands and wings, are full of eyes all around. Friend, you are NOT sneaking a cookie past them.

cards.question: The cherubim are covered in eyes all around, and so are their four ___.

cards.text: Ezekiel hears the wheels being called "the whirling wheels." And each of the cherubim has four faces.

cards.question: Each of the cherubim has four faces: a cherub, a man and two more. What are the other two?

cards.text: The cherubim rise upward, and Ezekiel says these are the same living creatures he had seen before. Hard to forget a face when there are four of them.

cards.question: Ezekiel had seen these living creatures before, by the River Kebar.

cards.text: When the cherubim move, the wheels move beside them, and even when they spread their wings to rise, the wheels stay right at their side. Put me next to a dance partner like that and I'd trip over my own gold base.

cards.question: When the cherubim stand still, the wheels stand still, and when the cherubim rise, the wheels rise with them. Why?

answers.text: the spirit of the creatures was in the wheels
the wheels were tied to their wings
the cherubim carried the wheels by hand

cards.text: And now the big moment. The glory of the LORD moves away from the threshold of the temple.

cards.question: The glory of the LORD moves away from the threshold of the temple and stands above the ___.

cards.text: As Ezekiel watches, the cherubim lift their wings and rise up from the ground, with the wheels right beside them. Then they stop.

cards.question: The cherubim rise from the ground with the wheels beside them. Where do they stop?

answers.text: the entrance of the east gate
the Fish Gate by the wall

cards.text: Ezekiel says it again: these are the living creatures he saw beneath the God of Israel by the River Kebar, and he knew they were cherubim.

cards.question: Ezekiel describes the cherubim one more time, and each one has six wings.

cards.text: Their faces look like the ones he saw by the River Kebar, and each creature goes straight ahead. Hold on to your apron, friend, because this vision isn't finished yet.
